summary: Our project is an interactive web application designed to visualize and analyze active fire hotspots across South America from 2018 to 2025. It integrates data from four NASA satellites: Aqua, Terra, NOAA-20, and Suomi-NPP, using MODIS and VIIRS sensors. The platform features interactive 2D and 3D maps, with filters by date, satellite, sensor system, and country. Designed for desktop computers, it aims to make satellite data easier to access, explore, and analyze through a friendly and intuitive user interface.
details: Our project is an interactive web application designed to display active fire hotspots across South America from 2018 to 2025, using data from four NASA satellites: Aqua, Terra, NOAA-20, and Suomi-NPP. Through interactive 2D and 3D maps and filters by date, satellite, sensor system, and country, users can easily visualize, explore, analyze, and collect hotspot data. The application is currently designed to run on desktop computers. We used Python for development, GitHub for version control and collaboration, and AI tools such as Gemini and Claude to support the development process. We focused on creating a friendly and intuitive user interface (UI), making the platform accessible and easy to navigate. Our goal is to simplify access to satellite information and help users better understand fire activity across South America.
